title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 210
paragraphs: Even so, he did not convince Xerxes, who let four days pass, expecting that the Greeks would take flight; but on the fifth day, when they still had not departed but remained — obstinate, as he thought, in their impudence and folly — he became enraged and sent the Medes and the Kissians against them, ordering that the men be taken alive and brought into his presence. When the Medes charged forward and attacked the Greeks, many of them fell, and others kept coming up continually, and they were not driven back, though they suffered heavy losses. They made it plain to everyone, and to the king himself not least, that human beings are many but men are few. This combat went on throughout the day.
